- src/rules/helpers/valid-story-reference-helpers.ts - JSDoc linked to 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION and REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY / REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION. - analyzeCandidateBoundaries(candidates, cwd): - Uses enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd) to classify each candidate as within or outside project root. - handleProjectBoundaryForExistence(...): - If candidates exist: - If hasOutOfProjectCandidate && !hasInProjectCandidate: calls reportInvalidPath({ storyPath, ... }) and returns true, ensuring existing files outside project are reported as invalidPath. - If existenceResult.status === "exists" and existenceResult.matchedPath is outside project root: calls reportInvalidPath and returns true. - performSecurityValidations(...): - If path.isAbsolute(storyPath) and allowAbsolute is false: reportInvalidPath and return false. - For paths containing traversal or separators, resolves to a full path and rejects with invalidPath when full is outside cwd.
- src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts - JSDoc tied to 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION and all key requirements. - Types: - StoryExistenceStatus = "exists" | "missing" | "fs-error" - StoryPathCheckResult, StoryExistenceResult, ProjectBoundaryCheckResult - enforceProjectBoundary(candidate, cwd): - Uses path.resolve for both cwd and candidate and sets isWithinProject when normalizedCandidate === normalizedCwd or startsWith(normalizedCwd + path.sep). - __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests(): clears an internal Map cache - buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - For paths starting with ./ or ../: candidates = [path.resolve(cwd, storyPath)] - For bare paths: - First candidate: path.resolve(cwd, storyPath) - Additional candidates: for each dir in storyDirs, path.resolve(cwd, dir, path.basename(storyPath)) - fileExistStatusCache: Map to cache filesystem checks - checkSingleCandidate(candidate): - Uses cache if present - try/catch around fs.existsSync and fs.statSync - Returns status "missing", "exists" (only if stat.isFile()), or "fs-error" with captured error - getStoryExistence(candidates): - Iterates candidates using checkSingleCandidate - Returns early on first "exists" with matchedPath - Otherwise returns first "fs-error" if any, else overall "missing" - storyExists(paths): - Calls getStoryExistence and returns status === "exists" (boolean API) - normalizeStoryPath(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs): - Builds candidates via buildStoryCandidates - Gets StoryExistenceResult, returns { candidates, exists, existence } - hasValidExtension(p): returns p.endsWith(".story.md")

Mapping to Acceptance Criteria and Requirements: - Core Functionality (valid @story paths to existing .story.md files): - normalizeStoryPath + buildStoryCandidates + getStoryExistence implement existence tracking. - hasValidExtension enforces .story.md when requireStoryExtension is true. - Tests validate both valid references and fileMissing/invalidExtension cases. - Quality Standards & Safe FS Operations: - All fs operations wrapped in try/catch (checkSingleCandidate); no uncaught errors. - Caching via fileExistStatusCache avoids redundant IO. - Integration with annotation format validation (005.0): - Rule scans comment nodes for lines starting with @story, compatible with the format-enforcement rule. - Uses context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(), following ESLint best practices. - User Experience (clear errors): - Messages fileMissing, invalidExtension, invalidPath, fileAccessError are specific and include the offending path and in fs-error cases the underlying error. - Tests assert correct messageIds and associated data. - Error Handling: - StoryReference utilities never throw on fs errors; instead they surface them as status "fs-error". - Rule converts fs-error into fileAccessError diagnostics with contextual error details. - Tests explicitly cover permission error (EACCES) and IO error (EIO) scenarios. - Documentation: - docs/rules/valid-story-reference.md provides path resolution rules, project boundary behavior, options, and examples consistent with the story.
- REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE: Implemented via checkSingleCandidate/getStoryExistence/normalizeStoryPath and enforced in reportExistenceStatus/reportExistenceProblems; covered by multiple tests named [REQ-FILE-EXISTENCE]. - REQ-ERROR-HANDLING: Implemented via fs-error status, fileAccessError diagnostics, and robust try/catch behavior; extensively tested in "Valid Story Reference Rule Error Handling". - REQ-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION: handleComment and validateStoryPath parse @story annotation lines from both line and block comments; tests demonstrate correct path extraction from comment-embedded @story lines. - REQ-PATH-RESOLUTION: buildStoryCandidates + normalizeStoryPath resolve relative and bare paths from cwd and configured storyDirectories; tests validate ./ prefix paths and use of storyDirectories. - REQ-SECURITY-VALIDATION: performSecurityValidations plus enforceProjectBoundary prevent unsafe absolute paths and traversal outside project root; tests for path traversal and absolute paths confirm behavior. - REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION: fileExistStatusCache with __resetStoryExistenceCacheForTests ensures cached IO; comments and implementation show caching used in all existence checks. - REQ-PROJECT-BOUNDARY: enforceProjectBoundary, analyzeCandidateBoundaries, and handleProjectBoundaryForExistence enforce that any resolved existing file outside the project is reported as invalidPath; tests explicitly exercise misconfigured storyDirectories and absolute paths outside project root. - REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATHS: Options storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, and requireStoryExtension are honored in create(); multiple tests under configurablePathsTester, allowAbsolutePathsTester, relaxedExtensionTester, and the configuration/boundary describe block confirm behavior.
traceability.notes: The `traceability/valid-story-reference` ESLint rule, its utilities, tests, and documentation collectively implement all acceptance criteria and detailed requirements of docs/stories/006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION.story.md. The rule validates that @story paths exist and have the correct extension, enforces project boundaries and security (no traversal or out-of-project access), supports configurable story directories and options, caches filesystem checks for performance, and exposes clear, specific diagnostics for missing files, invalid extensions, invalid paths, and filesystem errors. Comprehensive Jest tests tied directly to this story confirm correct behavior across normal, configuration, boundary, and error-handling scenarios, and all tests pass. Accordingly, this story is fully implemented.
